content:
Serving Runtime — Weekly Update (kernel work, KV cache, batching)
Date range: 2026-03-09 to 2026-03-13
Author: Ava Martinez (eng-serving-runtime)
Attendees: Ava, Ravi, Lena, Marcus, Sofia (sync notes + async standups included)

TL;DR:
- Kernel selection prototype for Falcon/LLAMA variants merged to branch and running perf smoke tests; 8–12% token latency improvement on A100 for 2k seq in priority paths. (see PR #412)
- KV cache correctness issues identified with multi-model routing; hotfix merged, further validation in progress. (JIRA-INF-2384)
- Dynamic batching improvements landed: adaptive timeout heuristic reduced average latency by ~6% on p95 in internal load tests. Further tuning needed for mixed sequence workloads.

Accomplishments this week:
- Kernel work:
  - Merged kernel selection shim that picks between optimized flash-attn kernel and fallback kernel based on sequence length + model architecture. Benchmark table in PR #412.
  - Added basic telemetry for kernel switch events (metrics emitted: kernel_choice, seq_len_bucket, model_tag). Telemetry stub in runtime; dashboards planned next sprint.
  - Ran end-to-end perf jobs for falcon-40b-instruct and llama-2-13b - results: flecked improvement on medium-length sequences (512–2k). Long tails still dominated by KV IO.

- KV cache:
  - Discovered race condition when routing requests across model variants: cache key normalization was missing model version tag, causing KV collisions under canary rollouts. Root cause in cache key building (see JIRA-INF-2384).
  - Hotfix applied to include model_version and routing_shard in cache key; hotfix PR #418 merged to main. Running validation across dedicated staging cluster.
  - Added unit tests simulating parallel canary rollout traffic; uncovered a second edge case for multi-tenant evictions. Filed follow-up (JIRA-INF-2410).

- Batching:
  - Adaptive batching timeout heuristic implemented: uses moving average of queue depth + recent latency to pick timeout. Reduced wasted cycles during low QPS.
  - Integrated batching heuristic with kernel selection (so certain kernels prefer smaller batches). Initial configs added to runtime config; tuning in progress.
  - Load test (mixed seq lengths, 30% long requests) shows p99 latency improved by ~4% and throughput stable. Observed a 10% CPU usage increase on batch manager side during peak — needs investigation.

Standup / daily log highlights:
- Mon 2026-03-09: Kernel selection prototype ready for review. KV team reproduces collision locally.
- Tue 2026-03-10: PR for kernel telemetry submitted. KV hotfix drafted. Batch heuristic prototype validated in sandbox.
- Wed 2026-03-11: Kernel PR merged to feature branch. KV hotfix merged to main (PR #418). Start long-run perf jobs.
- Thu 2026-03-12: Observed Kv eviction edge case under multi-tenant test; created follow-up ticket (JIRA-INF-2410). Batching config tuning reduced p95 for mixed workload.
- Fri 2026-03-13: Consolidated metrics and smoke test summary; preparing demo for platform-ops next week.

Blockers / Risks:
- KV eviction behavior under memory pressure is not fully understood for multi-tenant traffic; potential for transient correctness issues during rollouts. (Owner: Ravi)
- Kernel-specific regression on some Llama-derived models where the optimized kernel introduces small numerical differences that break exact logit constraints in the client. Need to decide acceptable tolerance or fallback. (Owner: Lena)
- Batch manager CPU spike during peak adaptive batching needs profiling; could impact SLOs if not mitigated. (Owner: Marcus)

Decisions / action items:
- Action: Run expanded KV-simulation harness across 5M simulated requests to validate eviction heuristics — Ravi, due 2026-03-20.
- Action: Add kernel numerical-tolerance test to CI for model onboarding to catch regressions early — Lena, due 2026-03-17.
- Action: Profile batch manager CPU, explore moving expensive ops off hot path (e.g., sampling heuristics) — Marcus, due 2026-03-18.
- Action: Platform-ops demo prep: include before/after perf graphs and show KV-hotfix scenario and recovery — Ava + Sofia, due 2026-03-16.

Meeting notes (sync 2026-03-11):
- Context: Quick sync to align kernel rollout with canary policy and KV fix.
- Notes:
  - Agreed to gate kernel rollout behind KV multi-tenant validation.
  - Canaries will run on 2 dedicated shards with telemetry flags enabled for 48h. If any correctness or >5% p95 regression observed, rollback automatically.
  - Add a runtime flag to force fallback kernel for selected tenants to speed rollback.
- Next check-in: 2026-03-18 deep-dive with perf and platform teams.

Files/links referenced:
- PR #412 (kernel selection): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412
- PR #418 (KV key hotfix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/418
- JIRA-INF-2384 (KV cache collision)
- JIRA-INF-2410 (KV eviction follow-up)
- Confluence: Serving Runtime Kernel & KV Design v2 (internal)

Notes to self / TODOs for next week:
- Finish extended KV sim, validate no cross-tenant collisions in 95th percentile scenarios.
- Push kernel telemetry dashboards to internal Grafana and add alert for kernel-choice sudden changes.
- Finalize batching config defaults for prod and document knobs in runtime-configs.md.

Appendix: quick perf numbers (internal smoke test)
- falcon-40b-instruct @ seq=1024: baseline p50 18ms -> optimized kernel p50 16ms (11% improvement)
- llama-2-13b @ seq=2048: baseline p95 245ms -> optimized 222ms (9% improvement)
- Mixed-workload batching test: p95 improved by ~6%, batch-manager CPU +10% during peak

If anything needs more detail, add comments below or DM in #eng-serving-runtime.
